mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines an element?

options.A: A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
options.B: A mixture of two or more substances.
options.C: A substance composed of two or more elements chemically combined.
options.D: A substance that can be separated by physical means.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
mcqs.explanation: An element is a pure substance consisting of only one type of atom and cannot be decomposed into simpler substances by chemical reactions. Options B, C and D describe mixtures, compounds, or physical separation, not elements.

mcqs.question: A compound is best described as:

options.A: A pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
options.B: A mixture of elements that can be separated by filtration.
options.C: An element that exists in more than one allotropic form.
options.D: A substance that cannot be broken down by any means.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds consist of two or more different elements chemically bonded in a definite ratio. They can be broken down only by chemical reactions. Options B, C and D are incorrect definitions.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an element from a compound?

options.A: Elements consist of only one type of atom, whereas compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded.
options.B: Elements are always gases, compounds are always solids.
options.C: Elements can be separated by physical methods, compounds cannot.
options.D: Elements have fixed composition, compounds have variable composition.

mcqs.answer: Elements consist of only one type of atom, whereas compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded.
mcqs.explanation: An element is made of a single kind of atom; a compound is formed when atoms of different elements combine chemically. Options B, C and D are misconceptions.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: Water (H₂O) is a compound. Which of the following statements reflects its fixed composition?

options.A: Each molecule of water always contains exactly two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
options.B: Water can contain varying numbers of hydrogen atoms.
options.C: The ratio of hydrogen to oxygen in water can change depending on temperature.
options.D: Water may sometimes consist of only hydrogen atoms.

mcqs.answer: Each molecule of water always contains exactly two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds have a definite stoichiometric ratio; for water it is always 2 H atoms to 1 O atom. Options B, C and D contradict the fixed composition principle.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly contrasts a compound with a mixture?

options.A: Salt (NaCl) – a compound; Air – a mixture.
options.B: Sugar (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) – a mixture; Brass – a compound.
options.C: Water (H₂O) – a mixture; Iron – a compound.
options.D: Carbon dioxide – a mixture; Sand – a compound.

mcqs.answer: Salt (NaCl) – a compound; Air – a mixture.
mcqs.explanation: NaCl is a chemical compound with fixed composition, while air is a physical mixture of gases. The other options misclassify substances.

mcqs.question: A student finds a pure sample that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by any chemical reaction. Which term best describes this sample?
mcqs.explanation: The description matches the definition of an element – a substance that cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances. Compounds can be broken down chemically, mixtures can be separated physically, and alloys are mixtures of metals.

mcqs.question: A student thinks that a compound is just a mixture of its constituent elements that can be separated by simple filtration. Which statement corrects this misconception?

options.A: Compounds are formed by chemical bonding of elements and cannot be separated by physical methods like filtration.
options.B: Compounds are mixtures that can be separated by filtration.
options.C: Elements are compounds that can be broken down by filtration.
options.D: All substances that can be filtered are compounds.

mcqs.answer: Compounds are formed by chemical bonding of elements and cannot be separated by physical methods like filtration.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds involve chemical bonds; separating them requires chemical reactions, not simple physical processes such as filtration. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: If a substance X cannot be broken down into simpler substances by any chemical reaction, but substance Y can be broken down into hydrogen and oxygen, which of the following correctly identifies X and Y?

options.A: X is an element; Y is a compound.
options.B: X is a compound; Y is an element.
options.C: Both X and Y are mixtures.
options.D: Both X and Y are elements.

mcqs.answer: X is an element; Y is a compound.
mcqs.explanation: Substance X fits the definition of an element (cannot be chemically decomposed). Substance Y can be decomposed into hydrogen and oxygen, indicating it is a compound (water, for example). Options B, C, and D misidentify the categories.
